description:
I'm a CSE student participating solo in NASA Space Apps 2026, taking on the Earth Information Jukebox challenge.

Multiverse Vendhan represents a king of infinite universes, inspired by the vastness of the cosmos and the pursuit of knowledge beyond our world.

My project aims to transform NASA Earth Information Center visualizations into real-time, data-driven sound, helping people experience and understand our changing planet in a new way.
summary:
PRITHVI is an interactive web experience developed for NASA Space Apps 2026's Earth Information Jukebox challenge. It uses NASA's Earth Information Center Climate Spiral (SVS #5190) and NASA GISTEMP v4 surface-temperature anomaly data as its primary case study.
The project connects scientific visualizations with deterministic, browser-generated sound. Selected temperature measurements and their changes over time are mapped to audio parameters such as pitch and rhythm, allowing users to explore Earth's changing systems through both sight and sound.
By combining interactive Earth visualization, scientific data exploration and real-time sonification, PRITHVI aims to make Earth science more engaging and accessible. It also explains the data sources, measurement units, baseline and sound-mapping methodology behind the experience.
details:
Project Overview

PRITHVI: The Sound of Earth is an interactive scientific experience developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 — The Earth Information Jukebox.

The project explores how Earth science visualizations can be paired with sound to create another way of understanding changes in our planet.

GitHub : https://github.com/vishanth14/Prithvi-The-Sound-of-Earth.git

How It Works

PRITHVI uses the NASA Earth Information Center Climate Spiral (NASA SVS #5190) and the underlying NASA GISTEMP v4 temperature-anomaly dataset as its primary case study.

Scientific observations are processed and validated before being passed through a documented sonification system. Temperature magnitude influences pitch, changes over time influence rhythm, and measurement variation influences the sound's timbre. The browser generates audio dynamically using Tone.js and the Web Audio API rather than relying on prerecorded music.

Users can explore the 3D Earth, inspect scientific visualizations, navigate the data timeline, listen to generated sound and understand how the measurements are translated into audio.

Technology

The application is developed using React, TypeScript, Three.js, React Three Fiber, GSAP, D3.js, PapaParse, Zod, Zustand, Tone.js and the Web Audio API.

Creativity and Impact

PRITHVI combines interactive planetary visualization, scientific storytelling and data-driven sonification in one experience. It aims to make complex Earth observations more engaging for students, educators and the general public, while offering an additional auditory perspective on scientific data.

The project distinguishes original scientific measurements from their normalized and sonified representations, with attention to source attribution, sampling limitations and accessibility.
